- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially after sharp spikes or corrections.
- Overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast window, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Tends to lag behind true price movements by 1–3 days, especially in downward trends.
- Shows persistent bias toward lower values when historical mean is high (e.g., >73), and overestimates when mean is low (e.g., <70).
- Underreacts to sudden price spikes; model often fails to capture the full magnitude of upward momentum.
- Overreacts to minor price drops; model frequently overshoots downward corrections.
- Mean reversion is not adequately modeled — model often holds onto overestimated values longer than true price reversion suggests.
- Horizon-specific: forecasts for 30-day windows are overly conservative in the first 10 days, then gradually adjust — but often too late to capture true trend shifts.
